name: TC-20-procurement-scenario
description: TC-20.3: Procurement End-to-End Scenario — MR → PR → PO → Receipt → Vendor Performance

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — Step 1: Maintenance Request (Parts Needed)
doc_metadata.caption: The procurement scenario starts when a maintenance request identifies parts that need to be purchased. The 'Create PR' server action initiates procurement.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — MR with Parts Requirements
doc_metadata.caption: The maintenance request identifies required parts and materials. After approval, the 'Create Purchase Request' action generates a PR with the correct items.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — Step 2: Purchase Request
doc_metadata.caption: The purchase request is generated from the MR. It contains the required items, quantities, and requestor information.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — PR from MR
doc_metadata.caption: The purchase request shows items needed for the maintenance work. After approval, a purchase order is created to send to the vendor.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — Step 3: Purchase Order
doc_metadata.caption: The purchase order is issued to the vendor based on the approved PR. The PO tracks delivery dates and payment terms.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — PO Issued to Vendor
doc_metadata.caption: The purchase order shows vendor details, line items, delivery schedule, and total amount. Approved POs become read-only.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — Step 4: Purchase Receipt
doc_metadata.caption: When goods arrive, a purchase receipt is recorded against the PO. This updates inventory and triggers vendor performance recalculation.

doc_metadata.title: TC-20.3 — Receipt & Vendor Update
doc_metadata.caption: The purchase receipt records the delivery date and quantities received. Vendor performance metrics (delivery rating, on-time rate) are automatically recalculated.
